title: An auditor's replay check

blocks.text: A state commission's auditor (in a fictional water utility's rate case) has the utility's stored record of the run behind its plan of record, and replays it. Each run record is a dictionary with a `snapshot` (the id of its inputs), its solver `settings`, the termination `status`, the `objective` value, and the `plan` (project id to start year). The auditor wants a list of what the replay did not reproduce.
Write `audit(original, replay, tol=1e-6)` in `audit.py`. It returns a list of findings, empty when the replay reproduced the run, in this order:

items: `"inputs differ"` when the snapshots differ. A replay of other inputs proves nothing about the run, so this is then the only finding.
`"settings differ: <names>"` with the setting names whose values differ, sorted and joined by `", "` (a setting only one run has differs too).

`"objective differs"` when the objectives are further apart than `tol` times the larger of 1 and the original's absolute value. Solvers compute in floating point, so two equal answers can differ in the last digits.
`"plan differs: <ids>"` with the project ids whose start years differ, sorted and joined by `", "`; a project in one plan only is one of them.

blocks.text: Before you code, decide which findings a replay with 8 threads instead of 1, the same objective and one project moved by a year should produce. The tests use hand-made run records. About fifteen lines.

cases.says: a replay equal in every field reproduces the run
each field that differs is reported, in the stated order
a replay of different inputs is reported as that alone
an objective within the tolerance counts as the same
a project funded in only one of the two plans is a plan difference

origin.section: Regulators Need Commitments Kept and a Result Anyone Can Reproduce

concepts: a regulator checks that a stored run is reproduced from its snapshot and settings, field by field
